enriched_description: Small New World monkey measuring 25-40 cm body length weighing 0.5-1 kg. Body covered with long beautiful dense fur in reddish-brown, gray, black, or orange coloration. Face bare with distinctive facial markings. Eyes forward-facing with large brown irises. Nose flat. Ears small and often tufted. Tail long and non-prehensile with bushy fur. Body small and compact. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. South American arboreal monkey with monogamous pair bonding.

New World monkey measuring 40-65 cm body length weighing 6-9 kg. Body covered with long black, brown, or reddish fur. Face bare and black with expressive features. Eyes forward-facing. Nose flat. Ears small. Tail extremely long and fully prehensile with bare tactile tip functioning as fifth limb. Limbs exceptionally long and slender. Body lightweight and agile. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Arboreal monkey of tropical America with brachiating locomotion.

Small New World monkey measuring 25-35 cm body length weighing 0.5-1.5 kg. Body covered with greenish-yellow fur with white ventral coloration. Face bare with distinctive black muzzle and white eye rings creating spectacle-like appearance. Eyes forward-facing with large brown irises. Nose flat. Ears small. Tail long and non-prehensile. Body small and slender. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Central and South American monkey with diurnal activity and large troop social structure.

Small lemur measuring 35-45 cm body length weighing 2-3.5 kg. Body covered with gray-brown fur with white underparts. Face white with black patches around eyes. Eyes large and forward-facing with amber irises. Nose wet and black. Ears large and pointed. Tail long with alternating black and white rings (12-13 bands). Body slender and agile. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Ring-tailed lemur of Madagascar with characteristic tail-raising posture.

Large lemur measuring 50-70 cm body length weighing 6-10 kg. Body covered with thick silky fur in black and white and fawn coloration. Face bare and black with small ears partially hidden in fur. Eyes large and forward-facing. Nose wet and black. Tail vestigial or absent (distinguishing from other lemurs). Body robust and stocky. Hind limbs elongated for vertical clinging and leaping. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Largest living lemur of Madagascar with haunting vocalizations.

Asian proboscidean measuring 250-300 cm at shoulder weighing 3000-5000 kg. Body massive with thick wrinkled gray-brown skin and sparse body hair. Head broad with twin-domed skull. Ears relatively small compared to African elephant. Trunk (proboscis) elongated and muscular with single finger-like projection at tip. Tusks present primarily in males, shorter than African species. Body barrel-shaped with arched back. Legs pillar-like with five toenails on forefeet. Tail long with terminal tuft. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, sparse hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart.

African proboscidean measuring 250-400 cm at shoulder weighing 4000-7000 kg. Body massive with thick wrinkled gray skin and sparse body hair. Head broad and single-domed. Ears enormous and flapping shaped like African continent. Trunk (proboscis) elongated and muscular with two finger-like projections at tip. Both sexes possess large ivory tusks curving outward. Body barrel-shaped with concave back. Legs pillar-like with four toenails on forefeet. Tail long with terminal tuft. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, sparse hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart.

Procyonid carnivore measuring 50-65 cm body length weighing 3-6 kg. Body covered with reddish-brown fur with black underparts and legs. Face white with reddish-brown tear markings below eyes. Ears pointed and white-edged. Tail long and bushy with alternating red and buff rings. Body slender and cat-like. Legs short with semi-retractile claws. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Old World raccoon-like carnivore of Himalayan and Chinese forests. Arboreal bamboo feeder.

Large procyonid measuring 120-190 cm body length weighing 70-125 kg. Body covered with distinctive black-and-white fur pattern: black limbs, shoulders, ears, and eye patches; white head, body, and rump. Face round with black eye patches. Ears rounded and black. Body robust and bear-like. Legs sturdy with modified wrist bone (radial sesamoid) functioning as pseudo-thumb. Tail short. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Herbivorous bear of Chinese bamboo forests.

Large marine fish measuring 60-150 cm with elongated streamlined body. Scales small and silvery with bluish-green dorsal coloration. Head elongated with prominent jaw bearing large fang-like teeth. Eyes large and lateral. Mouth wide with protruding lower jaw. Dorsal fins separated; first dorsal spiny, second dorsal soft-rayed. Anal fin similar to second dorsal. Tail forked. Lateral line prominent. Inherited vertebrate traits include bilateral symmetry, notochord-derived vertebral column, and gill respiration. Marine food fish of Australia, New Zealand, and southern Africa.
